people.jesus.role: Son of God and great high priest
people.jesus.relations: The writer calls him the Apostle and High Priest of our confession. He is the Son over God’s house.
people.jesus.meaning: The writer says the Son purified us of our sins. Then he sat down at the right hand of God. He was made like his brothers and suffered. So he can help those who are tempted. He offered himself once for all. He entered the holy place by his blood. The readers are told to look to Jesus and hold fast.
people.moses.role: Servant faithful in all God’s house
people.moses.relations: The writer names his law and the pattern for the tabernacle. He also names Moses leading out of Egypt.
people.moses.meaning: The writer says Moses was faithful as a servant in God’s house. Christ is faithful as a Son over it. Moses was warned to make the tabernacle by the pattern shown on the mountain. When grown, he refused to be called the son of Pharaoh’s daughter. He chose to share ill treatment with God’s people. He said he was terrified and trembling at the fearful sight.
people.aaron.relations: The writer names the order of Aaron. He also names Aaron’s rod that budded.
people.aaron.meaning: The writer says no one takes priestly honor for himself. He is called by God, as Aaron was. Christ did not glorify himself either. Aaron’s rod that budded is kept in the ark. The writer asks why another priest was needed. This priest is not called after the order of Aaron.
people.melchizedek.role: King of Salem and priest of God Most High
people.melchizedek.relations: He met Abraham and blessed him. Abraham gave him a tenth.
people.melchizedek.meaning: He met Abraham on his return from the slaughter of the kings. He blessed Abraham, and Abraham gave him a tenth. The writer says he is without father or mother. He has neither beginning of days nor end of life. Scripture says Christ is a priest forever after his order.
people.abraham.relations: He met Melchizedek, gave him a tenth, and offered up Isaac.
people.abraham.meaning: God swore to Abraham by himself, because no one was greater. Abraham went out when called, not knowing where he went. He gave Melchizedek a tenth. He offered up Isaac, his only born son. The writer says Christ helps the offspring of Abraham.
people.sarah.role: Wife who bore a child past age
people.sarah.relations: The writer says she counted the one who promised as faithful.
people.sarah.meaning: The writer says Sarah received power to conceive by faith. She bore a child when she was past age. She counted him faithful who had promised.
people.rahab.role: Prostitute who received the spies in peace
people.rahab.relations: She did not perish with those who were disobedient.
people.rahab.meaning: The walls of Jericho fell. The writer says Rahab the prostitute did not perish with the disobedient. She had received the spies in peace. The writer lists her among those who acted by faith.
people.timothy.relations: The writer calls him our brother. The writer hopes to see the readers with him.
people.timothy.meaning: In the closing notes, the writer says Timothy has been freed. If he comes soon, the writer will visit the readers with him. The letter says nothing more about him.
places.jericho.summary: The writer names Jericho in chapter 11. By faith its walls fell after they had been encircled for seven days. Rahab the prostitute, who received the spies, did not perish.
places.jericho.limits: The marker shows Tell es-Sultan. It does not give the date or cause of the walls’ fall.
sources.web.summary: The full text of Hebrews is the main text for the close readings.
sources.web.limits: The work does not name its writer. Authorship, dates, Greek forms, manuscripts, and the audience were not checked independently. Any archaeological picture of its tent description was not checked either. The comparisons give the writer’s own argument. They do not dismiss all Jewish worship. Heavenly Jerusalem has no marker on the earth.
sources.cfm-nt-2023-45.summary: The lesson links Christ’s suffering to help, open hearts, and called service.
sources.cfm-nt-2023-45.limits: Coverage follows the lesson’s text, not its title. Church uses for callings and ordinances are separate from independent historical evidence. The lesson names Paul, but that does not settle authorship. Linked videos, talks, and Restoration texts were not reviewed independently.
sources.cfm-nt-2023-46.summary: The lesson links ordinances to Christ and faith to trust in promises not yet fulfilled.
sources.cfm-nt-2023-46.limits: Coverage follows the lesson’s text, not its title. Church uses for callings and ordinances are separate from independent historical evidence. The lesson names Paul, but that does not settle authorship. Linked videos, talks, and Restoration texts were not reviewed independently.
sources.foskett-hebrews.summary: Foskett links the present readers to a long history of faithful endurance.
sources.foskett-hebrews.limits: This is Foskett’s own reading. Unnamed sufferers, authorship, the audience’s history, and Greek forms were not checked independently. She does not present endurance as approval of every kind of suffering.
sources.atlas-canaan.summary: This atlas from the Church shows towns and regions in Canaan.
sources.atlas-canaan.limits: The coordinates are estimates for display. A town marker does not prove each event in the text.
sources.lds-dc-128-fathers.summary: The section applies Paul’s words about the fathers to the living and the dead.
sources.lds-dc-128-fathers.limits: This is later Latter-day Saint scripture. It is a Church reading, apart from the words of the Bible passage.
chapters.*.mapNote: The Jericho marker shows Tell es-Sultan. The map gives no location to heavenly or unnamed settings.
chapters.*.routeEvidence: Hebrews names no travel route, so the map draws none.
